title: Choose PrepAhead's new look
question: Your steer: between Concourse Board and Line Map, with an identity. Two ways to cross them, one led by the line and one led by the board. This round's dealt forms lost to your steer; each left one rule behind.

options.label: The Lunch Line
options.lineage: a metro line diagram crossed with a split-flap departures board
options.thesis: PrepAhead is one green line: stalls are stops, every order rides it to collection, and the one number per screen clacks over in flip tiles.
materials: one green line with station rings
black flip tiles for one number
yellow lamp for now and new
options.viewport: Phone: SKIP THE LUNCH QUEUE, cut-off 10:00 in flip tiles, stalls as stops NS01 to NS04 on a green line. Tablet: 09 trays in flip tiles, a lunch line 11:30 to 13:30 whose stops grow with portions due, orders with four-stop progress.
options.risk: Two metaphors at once; it holds only if flip tiles stay on one number per screen.

raised.raise: Stops on the lunch line grow with the portions due in that slot.
Each slot has a capacity and cannot overflow, like a tape side.
The order list head names the span in view: 12:00 to 12:45.
Progress reads without colour: solid line done, dashed line still to come.
Every panel wears a small code tab (NS01) so stalls are findable at a glance.
After paying, the collection ticket owns the whole phone screen.

options.label: Departures
options.lineage: a split-flap departures board crossed with a metro line diagram
options.thesis: The canteen as a departures board: lunch slots leave on time, the trays number is the headline flap, and the green line tracks each order.
options.viewport: Phone: stalls as a black departures board with closing times in flip tiles. Tablet: a full-width board of pre-orders ranked by slot, each row with a lamp and a green progress line, 09 trays as the headline flap.
options.risk: More black on screen; reads transit first, lunch second.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Dozens of boxed modules with red tabs packed onto one screen.
options.viewport: A dense mosaic of stall and order modules.
options.kept: Every panel wears a small code tab.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Black text on a fixed measure, guide words naming the span in view.
options.kept: The list head names the span in view.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One stall fills the screen; flick to the next.
options.viewport: One stall per screen with a side rail of actions.
options.case: Needs food footage we don't have, and hides the stall list.
options.kept: The collection ticket owns the whole screen.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Lunch as side A and side B, timed so neither overflows.
options.viewport: Slots as tracklists timed to the tape.
options.kept: Slots have a capacity and cannot overflow.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Orders as stars, sized by magnitude, on a navy chart.
options.viewport: Lunch demand plotted as a constellation.
options.case: Poetic but slow to read at a counter.
options.kept: Dot size carries how much is due.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one rail; state is line form, not hue.
options.viewport: A charcoal plate with orders as hairlines on one rail.
options.case: Dark and technical; no identity a student would recognise.
options.kept: State reads as solid versus dashed line, not only colour.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A standard food-delivery app: white cards, dish photos, one brand colour.
canonCard.viewport: Search bar, category row, stall cards with photo, KPI tiles on the tablet.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every delivery app, and we have no real dish photos.
